source_row.item_data_json: {"options":{"A":"Causing bronchoconstriction, an effect essentially opposite to what this particular medication is actually intended to produce","B":"Thickening the client's mucus secretions further, rather than helping to break them down for easier clearance","C":"Breaking down the chemical structure of mucus, reducing its viscosity and making it easier to clear from the airways","D":"Having fairly little measurable effect on the actual consistency of the client's respiratory secretions"}}
source_row.rationale: Mucolytic agents like acetylcysteine work by breaking down the chemical structure of mucus (disrupting disulfide bonds in mucus glycoproteins), reducing its viscosity and making it easier to clear from the airways through coughing or suctioning.
